problem.text: A mathematical organization is producing a set of commemorative license plates. Each plate contains a sequence of five characters chosen from the four letters in AIME and the four digits in $2007$. No character may appear in a sequence more times than it appears among the four letters in AIME or the four digits in $2007$. A set of plates in which each possible sequence appears exactly once contains $N$ license plates. Find $\frac{N}{10}$.

steps.title: Where to start: find the one character that can repeat
steps.body: The available characters are A, I, M, E, 2, 0, 7. Each appears once in AIME or 2007, except $0$, which appears twice. So $0$ is the only character that may be used twice on a plate, and that is what makes counting awkward. The clean way is casework on how many $0$s the plate uses: none, one, or two.

your_turn.prompt: Apart from $0$, how many different characters are available, and how many times may each be used?
your_turn.answer: Six characters (A, I, M, E, 2, 7), each at most once.

steps.title: Cases with no $0$ and with one $0$
steps.body: With no $0$, all five characters are different and come from the six others: choose them in $\binom{6}{5} = 6$ ways and order them in $5! = 120$ ways, giving $720$ plates. With exactly one $0$, the plate has the $0$ plus four different characters from the other six, and again all five characters are different.

your_turn.prompt: How many plates have exactly one $0$?

steps.title: The case with two $0$s
steps.body: Now the plate has two $0$s plus three different characters from the other six, chosen in $\binom{6}{3} = 20$ ways. Careful: the five characters are not all different, so there are not $5!$ orders. Swapping the two $0$s gives the same plate, so we divide by $2!$.

your_turn.prompt: How many different orders are there of the characters $0, 0, A, I, M$?

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body:
The two-zero case gives $20\cdot 60 = 1200$ plates. Adding the three cases,
$$N = 720 + 1800 + 1200 = 3720,$$ so $\frac{N}{10} = 372$. The answer is **$372$**.
